content:
Yesterday we studied the beautiful history of Hobab. Moses invited him and said, "Come with us, and we will do thee good." At first Hobab refused and wanted to return to his own land and to his own family. But Moses pleaded with him again and promised that the goodness Yahweh would give to Israel would also be shared with him. Hobab was not an Israelite by birth. He was a Midianite. Yet he was invited to walk with the people of Yahweh and to share in the promise given to Israel. Later, his family line became connected with Israel and was known among the Kenites. They lived among Judah, showed kindness to Israel, and became part of Israel's story. Today we come to the lessons hidden in this history for us, the New Creation.

The first lesson comes from Hobab himself. We also were not Israelites according to the flesh. We were once strangers to the covenants and to the promises of Yahweh. But through Christ, the invitation came to us: "Come with us, and we will do thee good." We received a similar invitation through the Gospel and the letters of the Apostles & disciples, to leave our old nature, our old life, and our old ways, and to journey with the people of God toward the promised Kingdom. And like Hobab, many of us also hesitated at first. The old life was familiar. The world was familiar. Old traditions were familiar. Family ways were familiar. Everything behind us was known, and the journey ahead was unknown. But the call of Yahweh was greater than the comfort of the old life. So, we accepted the invitation and began to walk with the flock of Christ through the wilderness of this present world. This is where every one of us began; with an invitation that called us out of what was familiar and into a journey of faith.

The next lesson comes from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab. They teach us that those who join themselves to Yahweh's people must become faithful companions in the journey. They were not merely visitors passing through. They became connected with Judah and lived among the people of God.
This shows us that the New Creation must not only hear the invitation but also join the journey fully. We must not stand outside and watch from a distance. We must walk, we must serve, we must endure, and we must remain faithful together with the people of God. It is not enough to have once said yes to the invitation. The Kenites did not simply accept and then wander back to their own land. They stayed. They belonged. They shared the road with Israel through all its difficulties. And in the same way, we are called not just to begin the journey, but to walk it faithfully to the end, joined truly to the flock of Christ.

Then we see Jael, who came from this same Kenite family. She was the wife of Heber the Kenite, from the children of Hobab. When Sisera, the enemy commander, fled from the battle, Jael acted with courage. She did not remain passive when the enemy of Yahweh came near her tent. By her hand, Sisera was destroyed, and Israel received deliverance. Jael teaches the New Creation courage. We are not called to be weak or timid in the face of the enemy. We are soldiers of Christ. We must stand firmly against sin, against false doctrine, against fear, and against the works of darkness. And notice what Jael used;
a tent peg and a hammer, simple things that were already in her hand. Likewise, Yahweh can use whatever is in our hand if we are faithful. We may think our strength is small, our gift is small, our ability is small. But obedience in the right moment can bring a great victory. Jael did not have a sword or an army.She had what was near her, and she used it faithfully when the moment came.

The next lesson comes from the memory of the Kenites in the days of Saul. When Saul went to judge Amalek, he warned the Kenites to separate themselves from the Amalekites, because they had shown kindness to Israel when Israel came out of Egypt. Their kindness, shown generations earlier,
was not forgotten. This teaches us that the New Creation must be a people of kindness. We must help the journey of God's people, not hinder it. We must not be a burden to the flock, but a support to it. And here is a comforting truth; kindness shown in the wilderness may be remembered by Yahweh even many generations later. Nothing that is done for His people is ever wasted.The smallest kindness, the quiet help offered to a fellow traveller, the support given when it was needed, is seen by God and treasured by Him. The Kenites showed kindness when Israel was weak and newly out of Egypt, and centuries later that kindness still stood to their account.

Then we come to the Rechabites. The Rechabites were praised in the days of Jeremiah because they obeyed the command of their father Jonadab.
They refused wine and lived in separation according to the instruction that had been given to them. Yahweh used their obedience as a witness against Judah, because the Rechabites obeyed their earthly father, but Judah had not obeyed Yahweh. The Rechabites teach the New Creation obedience and separation.We must be a people who listen and who obey. We must not be carried away by the customs and the spirit of the world around us. And there is a searching comparison here. If an earthly family command was obeyed so faithfully by the Rechabites, generation after generation, how much more should we obey the voice of Yahweh, our heavenly Father? Their faithfulness to a man's word puts to shame any half-hearted obedience to the living God. They stand as a quiet rebuke and a shining example to all who claim to follow God.

So, in Hobab and his descendants, we see four beautiful characters set before us. In Hobab, we see a man invited to leave his old life and join the journey of Yahweh's people. In the Kenites, we see faithful companions who lived among Judah and showed kindness to Israel. In Jael, we see courage to stand against the enemy. And in the Rechabites, we see obedience, separation, and faithfulness carried across many generations. These are the very characters that must be found in the New Creation. Each one is a piece of what we are called to be. Not one of them stands alone; together they form a picture of the faithful believer who has answered the invitation of Yahweh.

And so the calling is clear before us. We have accepted the invitation, and now we must walk faithfully. We must be useful in the wilderness journey, as Hobab could be eyes for Israel. We must be faithful companions who truly belong among the people of God, as the Kenites did. We must show kindness to the flock, knowing it is remembered by Yahweh. We must be courageous against the enemy, using whatever is in our hand, as Jael did. And we must obey the voice of Yahweh and remain separated from the spirit of the world, as the Rechabites did across their generations. Moses said to Hobab, "Come with us, and we will do thee good." Today that same invitation has reached us through Christ & his servants. We have come out of the old land, and we have come to share in the blessings of Yahweh. Now let us walk the whole journey faithfully, until we reach the promised Kingdom to which the cloud is leading us still.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We thank You that the invitation once given to Hobab has now reached us through Christ.

We were strangers to Your covenants, yet You called us to come and share in Your goodness.

Make us faithful companions who truly belong among Your people, and never merely watch from outside.

Give us the courage of Jael to stand against the enemy with whatever You have placed in our hand.

Make us kind to the flock, and let no kindness done for Your people be counted as wasted.

And give us the obedience of the Rechabites, that we may listen to Your voice above every other.

Keep us separated from the spirit of the world, and faithful to the very end of the journey.

In the name of Christ, who invited us to come, we pray. Amen.
